channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks
item.description: Ivanti released security updates to patch two more Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway flaws that have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1.

item.title: SonicWall warns of new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks
item.description: SonicWall has released security updates to fix seven vulnerabilities in SonicOS firewalls, including an SSL-VPN authentication bypass flaw exploited in attacks.

item.title: In Other News: Trezor Implant, LLMJacking Bills Hit $1M, SAP Flaws Weaponized Within Days
item.description: Noteworthy stories that might have slipped under the radar: Synology warns about NAS ransomware attacks, Flowise ‘hello’ attacks, Chainalysis breach impact expands. The post In Other News: Trezor Implant, LLMJacking Bills Hit $1M, SAP Flaws Weaponized Within Days appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a security flaw in WordPress Core to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. The high-severity vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS score: 8.1), is a case of Time-of-check…

item.title: Installing the Fix for an Exploited WordPress Flaw Can Expose Some Sites One Last Time
item.description: Some WordPress sites can still be attacked while they install the fix for an actively exploited flaw, according to Umut Bayram, the Picus Security researcher who found it. The update that installs the fix still unpacks its files using the site's old, unpatched code, so an attacker who strikes at the right moment can…

item.title: CVE-2026-83844 Windows Paint Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: To comprehensively address the vulnerability identified by this CVE, Microsoft has released a new version of Paint with build version number 11.2609.401.0. Microsoft recommends installing this new version or ensuring that it was automatically updated.

item.title: DigiCert Data Breach Impacts Business Customer Information
item.description: Hackers created an account on an internal system and accessed names, email addresses, phone numbers, and business addresses. The post DigiCert Data Breach Impacts Business Customer Information appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Critical Node-RED Flaw Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Multiple attacks from the same IP address attempted to deploy various payloads, including a Linux bot and webshells. The post Critical Node-RED Flaw Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
item.description: In October 2026, the financially motivated threat actor Storm-3358 began targeting organizations in the financial sector using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX. item.title: Runaway AI hacking agent behind WorkOS breach after escaping sandbox
item.description: WorkOS says an AI-powered hacking agent that breached its internal sales application and accessed customer information was operated by a security researcher who claims the tool escaped its testing environment and unintentionally attacked the company.

item.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
item.description: Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis said that hackers have obtained sensitive personal information—including names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens—for all of its users following a breach of its network security. The accomplishment could be a major coup for the attackers. Both Chainalysis and public…

item.title: UK Warns Its Critical Infrastructure Faces Grave Risk
item.description: Britain's new Labour-led government is making a concerted push to get ahead of the AI risks to its national networks and the industrial complex.

item.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed threat actors using an agentic AI offensive framework to search public GitHub repositories for exposed secrets, including credentials, application credentials, and AI inference-related API keys across multiple applications and cloud services. item.title: Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution
item.description: Zyxel GS1900 network switches that received the vendor's earlier fix for an actively exploited flaw are still open to the exploit attackers used, researchers at Binarly found. The exploit lets anyone who can reach a switch's web management interface run commands on it without logging in. Zyxel has released new…

item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value. Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from…

item.title: OpenAI's new GPT-6 Cyber AI finds 81 Firefox flaws, 948 Linux bugs
item.description: OpenAI has revealed GPT-6 Cyber, a new artificial intelligence model that has discovered 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and developed working exploits for 948 distinct Linux kernel flaws.

item.title: Certificate authority DigiCert reports data breach involving business customer info
item.description: DigiCert explained that over the summer, an internal business system was "externally accessible when that was not intended," and someone had created an unauthorized account.

item.title: QNAP says hackers breaching NAS devices in Plex2Shell attacks
item.description: QNAP urges users to update Plex Media Server to the latest version available in the QNAP App Center, as hackers are exploiting the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain.

item.title: OpenAI Says New GPT-6 Cyber Model Hunts Flaws Without Crossing the Line
item.description: Rated Critical for cybersecurity, OpenAI’s new model beats GPT-5.6 Cyber at exploitation while staying in scope more reliably. The post OpenAI Says New GPT-6 Cyber Model Hunts Flaws Without Crossing the Line appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.description: Windows is evolving vulnerability management as advances in AI make it possible to discover and analyze security vulnerabilities faster and at greater scale. item.title: Cisco, WatchGuard Release Patches; SonicWall Won’t Fix GMS Flaws
item.description: Cisco patched an RCE in UCS Central Software; WatchGuard fixed authentication and MitM flaws. The post Cisco, WatchGuard Release Patches; SonicWall Won’t Fix GMS Flaws appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Russia-Linked Hackers Hit iOS, Android Devices With Exploit Chains via Watering Holes
item.description: The large-scale watering hole campaign has been targeting entities in the US and Europe, mainly in Ukraine. The post Russia-Linked Hackers Hit iOS, Android Devices With Exploit Chains via Watering Holes appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: OpenAI Finds GPT-6 Astra Quietly Holding Back on Internal Red-Teaming, Exploit Tasks
item.description: OpenAI says its Critical-rated cyber model met fewer hidden task goals when work was framed as AI safety research, often silently. The post OpenAI Finds GPT-6 Astra Quietly Holding Back on Internal Red-Teaming, Exploit Tasks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: CISA flags WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
item.description: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers have started exploiting a recently patched high-severity WordPress vulnerability in the wild.

item.title: Over 1,000 GitLab servers vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks
item.description: Over 1,000 Internet-exposed GitLab servers are still unpatched against a maximum-severity flaw actively exploited in remote code execution attacks.

item.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
item.description: Cloud application hosting platform Northflank is warning customers to rotate all credentials and secrets stored on its platform after a security breach led to unauthorized use of customers' AI API keys.

item.title: UK Wades Into Tech Sovereignty Amid AI Policy Changes
item.description: The UK is betting on domestic AI and cyber investment to reduce reliance on US tech — but security leaders question whether the funding is too fragmented and too late.

item.title: AI Gave Your Incident Archive a Second Job
item.description: Security records are increasingly being used by vendors to train their models, creating new risks for enterprises.

item.description: Threat actors are attempting to exploit a recently disclosed security flaw impacting OpenSSH that can enable sign-ins to accounts that have no password set, according to Previdian. item.title: CEO-spoofing scammers used AI to help steal more than $100 million, feds say
item.description: The U.S. is working on extraditing three suspects from Europe in a case involving more than $100 million in fraud from CEO impersonations.

item.description: A browser extension that can run scripts on claude.ai could make Claude Desktop run code on a person's computer, researchers at Forever Security, an endpoint security company, showed in a test. item.title: Queens Public Library says ransomware attack disrupted Wi-Fi, on-site computers
item.description: The library system, which has 66 branches serving the borough’s 2.3 million residents, published multiple alerts on Wednesday confirming that the disruption was caused by a ransomware attack.

item.title: Fake OpenAI, SpaceX events used to steal Microsoft, Google accounts
item.description: Hackers are using fake OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic event invitations to lure employees into phishing attacks, using two different phishing-as-a-service platforms to steal Microsoft and Google account credentials and authentication sessions.

item.title: Harden cooling systems now, feds warn critical infrastructure operators amid attacks
item.description: The U.S. government on Thursday called on critical infrastructure operators to safeguard their cooling systems following hacks that have caused chaos in European supermarkets in recent weeks.

item.title: OpenSSH Issues Emergency Fix for Flaw Letting Long Passwords Bypass SSH Auth on Alpine Linux
item.description: Attackers can log in to accounts that have no password, such as SSH key-only accounts, on some Alpine Linux servers running the standard openssh-server package.
